samples.summary: v1 auth summary in the design doc still describes the OLD API-key contract (scope match only, membership checked for JWT only)
samples.evidence: docs/design/rest-api.md:158-161 — "All endpoints are prefixed with `/api/v1/` and protected by `CombinedAuthGuard`. For API key auth, the `:workspaceId` parameter must match the key's bound workspace. For JWT auth, workspace membership is checked via `WorkspaceService.assertMember()`." After this change (packages/backend/src/api/v1/workspace-scope.guard.ts:40-45) an API key ALSO goes through `assertMember`, and the sentence's explicit JWT-vs-key contrast now reads as the guarantee it used to be. The later folders section (rest-api.md:524-534) documents the new rule correctly, so the two halves of the same doc disagree. Fix belongs in the doc, not the guard.

samples.summary: Folder rename/move/delete authorization now exists in two hand-written copies (web JWT controller and the new v1 controller) that can drift
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/folder/folder.controller.ts:74-119 (`PATCH folders/:id`, `DELETE folders/:id`) repeats, line for line, the manager gate, the `assertSameWorkspace` + `assertNoCycle` ordering and the two error strings that the new packages/backend/src/api/v1/folders.controller.ts:110-155 now also contains. Only `FolderService` is shared, not the policy: the v1 copy additionally scopes lookups to the route workspace (`folderInWorkspace`, 404 for a foreign folder) while the web copy has no workspace in its path at all, so a future policy change made in one place silently leaves the other behind. No test compares the two.

samples.summary: Every API-key request on all 14 v1 controllers now pays two extra DB round-trips per call, including the hot per-cell/per-image routes
samples.evidence: workspace-scope.guard.ts:44 now always calls `assertMember`, and `WorkspaceService.assertMember` (packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.service.ts:236-243) itself re-runs `resolveId(workspaceId)` on an id the guard already resolved at line 37, then a `workspaceMember.findUnique`. Consumers that were not in the diff and are explicitly throttled for burst traffic now absorb this per request: packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts (scripted cell writes), packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:22 and packages/backend/src/api/v1/image-read.controller.ts:42 (`@Throttle({ limit: 600/min })`, one request per embedded image, plus the same pair added by hand at image-read.controller.ts:108). Passing the already-resolved id to a lookup that skips `resolveId` would remove half of it.

samples.summary: CLI agent skills were not updated for the new `docs copy` / `docs move` commands and there is no folders skill
samples.evidence: packages/cli/skills/docs-manage.md:5-10 declares the namespace's tool list as exactly `docs list|create|get|rename|delete`; the two new subcommands registered in packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:174 and :196 are absent, and no `folders-*.md` skill exists (packages/cli/skills/ holds 18 files, indexed by SKILL.md:49). Nothing in scripts/agent enforces these lists (they are prose loaded as corpus, scripts/agent/charters/charters.json:24), so this only means an agent reading the skills will not discover the capability — the CLI schema registry does carry them.

finding.summary: API-key image read bypasses the delta's new "a key dies with its minter's membership" invariant
finding.evidence: `ApiV1ImageReadController` is the only v1 controller in `api-v1.module.ts:45-61` that does NOT mount `WorkspaceScopeGuard` (it mounts `OptionalCombinedAuthGuard` only, image-read.controller.ts:41) and resolves access by hand. Its API-key branch — image-read.controller.ts:96-99 — returns as soon as `user.workspaceId === resolvedWorkspaceId`, with no `assertMember(resolvedWorkspaceId, Number(user.id))` call. The delta's whole premise (workspace-scope.guard.ts:14-20: "removing somebody from a workspace would otherwise leave every key they ever minted working with full workspace authority") therefore does not hold for `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images/:imageId`: a key minted by a user who has since been removed from the workspace still reads every workspace image. Fix belongs at image-read.controller.ts:96 (add the membership check to the API-key branch, falling through to the share-token path the same way the JWT branch does at lines 100-113).

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence is factually wrong about the code. It claims the API-key branch in `assertCanRead` "returns as soon as `user.workspaceId === resolvedWorkspaceId`, with no `assertMember(...)` call". In fact image-read.controller.ts:97-113 only *throws* on scope mismatch (98-100) and then falls through to `await this.workspaceService.assertMember(resolvedWorkspaceId, Number(user.id))` at 108-111 before returning at 112 — the identical pair of checks WorkspaceScopeGuard performs at workspace-scope.guard.ts:40-44. `WorkspaceService.assertMember` (workspace/workspace.service.ts:236-243) throws ForbiddenException when no membership row exists, so a key minted by a since-removed member is rejected on GET /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images/:imageId. The guard's doc comment explicitly notes this controller repeats the two checks by hand (workspace-scope.guard.ts:24-26), and the behaviour is covered by tests at image-read.controller.spec.ts:164-185 (member minter -> served, assertMember called with ('w1',7)) and 190-211 ("forbids an API key whose minter is no longer a member, token or not"). The only accurate observation — that this controller mounts only OptionalCombinedAuthGuard (image-read.controller.ts:41) and is not in the WorkspaceScopeGuard set in api-v1.module.ts:45-61 — yields no bypass, since the manual path enforces the same invariant. The proposed fix is already implemented at the very line cited.
